items.title: Developer interface
items.text: A developer enters an SQL request: show students whose ClassID is '7A'.

items.title: Query processor
items.text: The DBMS takes the request and prepares it for execution.

items.title: Answer
items.text: The system returns Noor and Tahir, the two students in 7A.

details.title: Inside the query processor — two routes
details.text: For a structure command such as CREATE TABLE, the DDL interpreter processes its definition and records metadata in the data dictionary. For a data command such as SELECT, the DML compiler translates and optimises the request; the query evaluation engine executes it. You will learn the exact SQL commands in the next section.
details.uz: Developer interface — so'rov yoziladigan joy. Query processor — so'rovni bajarishga tayyorlaydi va natija olishda ishlaydi.

details.title: Activity 8F: apply the whole idea
details.text: In a timetable system, the DBMS must restrict pupils to their permitted records, allow teachers appropriate access, and let administrators update authorised schedules. An audit log can record changes, while scheduled backups help recover lost timetable data.
details.uz: Har bir vositaning vazifasini ajrating: ruxsat, maxfiylik, tiklash, tekshirish.

worked.prompt: Activity 8F adaptation: explain why the school needs both access rights and backups.
worked.answer: Access rights limit which users can read or change particular data. Backups provide a recovery copy if data is lost or corrupted. A permission rule cannot restore deleted data; a backup does not prevent unauthorised access to the live database.
criteria: Relate each control to a different risk.

checks.prompt: The database is damaged by an accidental deletion. Which feature helps restore earlier data?
checks.why: A backup provides a recovery copy. An audit trail can help investigate what happened.

checks.prompt: A developer submits SELECT to show 7A students. Explain what the developer interface and query processor each do.
checks.answer: The developer interface accepts the SQL request. The query processor uses its DML compiler to prepare and optimise the query, then its query evaluation engine executes it and retrieves the selected data.
criteria: Mention execution by the evaluation engine.

lessons.title: SQL: structure or stored data?
lessons.subtitle: Choose the job, command and data type.
objectives: Classify SQL as DDL or DML.
Choose suitable attribute data types.
Explain the purpose of an SQL script.
lessons.hook: Is adding a new column the same kind of operation as adding a new student?

blocks.title: Add a column or add a student?
blocks.text: SQL is Structured Query Language. Data definition language (DDL) defines structures. Data manipulation language (DML) works with stored data. In Hodder’s classification, SELECT also belongs to DML.
blocks.uz: Yangi Email ustuni ochish — jadval tuzilishini o‘zgartirish, ya’ni DDL. Yangi o‘quvchi qatorini kiritish — ma’lumot bilan ishlash, ya’ni DML. SELECT ma’lumotni o‘zgartirmasa ham bu kitobda DML ga kiradi.
blocks.remember: DDL: table structure. DML: data in the table.

blocks.title: Each field needs a suitable type
blocks.text: Choose the type for what the value means. A student ID is text even when it contains digits; we do not add two student IDs together.
blocks.uz: Tur qiymatning ma’nosiga qarab tanlanadi. StudentID ichida raqamlar bor, lekin u bilan hisoblamaymiz. Shuning uchun text turi mos. CHAR uzunligi belgilangan; VARCHAR esa belgilangan maksimumgacha turli uzunlikda bo‘ladi.

blocks.title: Recognise the command’s job
rows: Create or change a table definition
blocks.text: Name the intended change before choosing the command. Removing rows with DELETE keeps the table definition.
blocks.uz: Avval nimani qilmoqchi ekaningizni ayting, keyin buyruqni tanlang. DELETE qatorlarni o‘chiradi; jadvalning tuzilishi qoladi.

blocks.title: Save commands as an SQL script
blocks.text: A script is a saved sequence of SQL commands. For example, create Teacher first, then Class, then Student. Saving the sequence makes the setup reusable. Commands still need to match the current database state and the chosen DBMS.
blocks.uz: Bir nechta SQL buyrug‘ini tartibi bilan faylga saqlasak, SQL script bo‘ladi. Keyin shu ishni qayta bajarish mumkin. Ammo mavjud jadvalni yana yaratish kabi buyruqlar joriy holatga mos kelishi kerak.

worked.prompt: Add a Phone column, then store Noor’s phone number. Are these the same SQL job?
worked.answer: Adding the column changes the structure: DDL. Storing the phone number changes a row’s data: DML. The phone number is text because leading zeroes and symbols may matter.

checks.prompt: ALTER TABLE Student ADD Email VARCHAR(120) is…
options: DDL because it changes the structure
checks.why: The command defines a new column, rather than inserting a row.

checks.prompt: Why store StudentID S1276 as text?
options: It identifies a student and includes a letter
checks.why: The ID is a label, not an amount for arithmetic. Text preserves its format.

recap: DDL: table structure. DML: data in the table.
lessons.mistake: Do not choose INTEGER simply because an identifier contains digits.
lessons.next: Next: Create a table one line at a time.

details.title: The two jobs of SQL
rows: Change a value in Noor's row

details.title: Look at a small table definition
details.note: DDL defines two columns and the primary key. This is a teaching subset; the complete school design comes later.

details.title: Now put one row into the table
details.text:
INSERT INTO Student (StudentID, FirstName)
VALUES ('S1276', 'Noor');
details.note: DML adds data to the existing table; it does not create new columns.

details.title: Every command on Hodder's list
Choose a suitable data type — Table 8.14
An SQL script is a reusable set of commands
details.text: An SQL script is a list of SQL commands for one task, often saved to a file. The database structure must be defined before rows can be added to it. SQL syntax and type handling differ slightly between database products; the following exercises label important SQLite/MySQL differences.
details.uz: SQL bir xil til bo'lsa ham ikkita vazifani bajaradi: DDL — jadval tuzilishi; DML — jadval ichidagi ma'lumot.

details.title: Dialect note
details.text: SQL implementations differ. CHARACTER length syntax, BOOLEAN storage and schema-alteration support vary by DBMS. The examples below identify portable design intent and separately flag commands SQLite does not support. Use the selected DBMS’s syntax rather than copying a malformed printed example.
details.uz: DDL — tuzilma bilan; DML — saqlangan ma’lumot bilan ishlaydi. Yangi ustun qo‘shish va yangi qator qo‘shish ikki xil vazifa.

worked.prompt: Choose types for StudentID S1276, FirstName Noor, DateOfBirth, ExamMark 78 and ConsentGranted. Explain one choice.
worked.answer: CHAR(5) or VARCHAR(5), VARCHAR(40), DATE, INTEGER, BOOLEAN. StudentID is text because it includes a letter and is an identifier rather than a number to calculate with.

checks.prompt: A school creates a new Teacher table. Which command is appropriate?
checks.why: CREATE TABLE defines a table. INSERT INTO adds a row to a table that already exists.

checks.prompt: Choose a type for StudentID S1276, DateOfBirth 2010-09-22 and ExamMark 80. Explain why StudentID should not be INTEGER.
checks.answer: StudentID: VARCHAR(5) or suitable CHARACTER; DateOfBirth: DATE; ExamMark: INTEGER. StudentID includes a letter and is an identifier, not a number for arithmetic.

lessons.title: Create a table one line at a time
lessons.subtitle: A small table, a link, then the full school design.
objectives: Read and write CREATE TABLE definitions.
Declare primary and foreign keys.
Explain CREATE DATABASE and ALTER TABLE.
lessons.hook: How can the DBMS stop a student from referring to a class that does not exist?

blocks.title: Build a small table first
blocks.note: CREATE TABLE gives the table its name. Inside the brackets, each line defines a column. StudentID stores text and is the required unique key. FirstName stores text. The comma separates the definitions; the semicolon ends the command.
blocks.uz: Avval ikki ustunli kichik jadval: nomi LessonStudent. StudentID — matn va primary key; FirstName — ism saqlaydigan matn. NOT NULL qiymat bo‘lishi shartligini bildiradi. Har bir satr nima ish qilishini tushunib oling.

blocks.title: Now give each student a class
blocks.note: Create the referenced class table first. In LessonMember, FOREIGN KEY (ClassID) names the local column. REFERENCES LessonClass(ClassID) names the table and key it must match. Merely using the same column name does not enforce a relationship.
blocks.uz: Avval sinflar jadvalini yaratdik. Keyingi jadvaldagi ClassID unga murojaat qiladi. FOREIGN KEY — shu jadvaldagi ustun; REFERENCES — qaysi jadvalning qaysi kalitiga bog‘lanishi. Bir xil nom yozishning o‘zi yetmaydi.

blocks.title: The pair, not each column, is unique
blocks.note: This small example isolates the composite-key rule. StudentID may repeat and SubjectName may repeat, but the same pair may not repeat. The full school definition below adds the foreign keys as well.
blocks.uz: Bu kichik misolda faqat composite key qoidasiga qarang. StudentID takrorlanishi mumkin; SubjectName ham. Lekin aynan bitta juftlik takrorlanmaydi. To‘liq maktab sxemasida ikkalasi foreign key ham bo‘ladi.

blocks.title: Read the full school definition one table at a time
blocks.text: You have now seen the three building blocks: a column with a type, a primary key, and a foreign-key reference. Open the complete school SQL below to see Teacher, Class, Student, Subject and StudentSubject built from those same parts.
blocks.uz: Endi uch bo‘lak tanish: ustun va turi, primary key, foreign key. Quyidagi batafsil bo‘limda to‘liq maktab SQL i bor. Har bir jadvalda aynan shu bo‘laklarni topib o‘qing. SQLite da foreign key larni sinashdan oldin PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON yoqiladi.

worked.prompt: Read FOREIGN KEY (ClassID) REFERENCES Class(ClassID) in ordinary words.
worked.answer: The ClassID value in this table must refer to a ClassID that exists in Class (unless NULL is allowed). The first ClassID is local; Class(ClassID) names the referenced table and column.

checks.prompt: Which part states the parent table and key?
checks.why: REFERENCES identifies the referenced table and key; FOREIGN KEY identifies the local columns.

checks.prompt: Which definition prevents duplicate student–subject pairs?
checks.why: The composite primary key makes the pair unique while allowing either column to repeat.

recap: Create referenced structures and compatible keys.
PK identifies; FK ... REFERENCES connects.
Check DBMS-specific CREATE DATABASE and ALTER TABLE support.
lessons.mistake: Creating a foreign-key-looking column name alone does not enforce referential integrity; declare the constraint.
lessons.next: Next: SELECT: build one question at a time.

details.title: Step 1 — create the Class table
details.note: ClassID is unique, so it is the primary key. This first example contains only two columns.

details.title: Step 2 — create Student and link it to Class
details.note: FOREIGN KEY names Student's own column; REFERENCES names the table and parent key that must match.

details.title: Read each line of that command
rows: StudentID is short text and uniquely identifies rows
This is the linking column in Student
Look for a matching primary key in Class

details.title: Test the rule with three simple cases

items.title: Class 7A already exists
items.text: Student.ClassID = '7A' can be accepted if other constraints are satisfied.

items.title: Class 9Z does not exist
items.text: The DBMS can reject the non-null foreign-key value because it has no matching Class row.

items.title: More than one student in 7A
items.text: This is valid: foreign-key values may repeat in Student even though Class.ClassID is unique.

details.title: Step 3 — Hodder Activity 8G: add Teacher
details.note: This is a fresh, expanded version of Class, not a command to run after the Step 1 CREATE TABLE. The teacher is created first; Class holds the linking foreign key.

details.title: Step 4 — change an existing structure
details.note: Hodder Table 8.13 also names CREATE DATABASE and ALTER TABLE. CREATE DATABASE is not supported by SQLite. Add-primary-key and add-foreign-key ALTER syntax varies by DBMS, so declare keys within CREATE TABLE for the runnable exercises.

details.title: Complete 3NF design uses five tables
details.text: Once the simple link is understood, the full school model has Teacher, Class, Student, Subject and StudentSubject. StudentSubject uses a composite PRIMARY KEY (StudentID, SubjectName), with separate foreign keys to Student and Subject. These extra tables were introduced during 8.1 normalisation; you do not need to memorise five CREATE TABLE scripts before understanding one.
details.uz: Birinchi ikki jadvalni tushuning: Class — asosiy jadval, Student — unga ClassID orqali bog'langan. Keyin Teacher qo'shiladi.

details.title: First create the referenced Teacher table
Then create Class and Student
details.text:
CREATE TABLE Class (
  ClassID VARCHAR(4) NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
  Location VARCHAR(60),
  LicenceNumber INTEGER NOT NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY (LicenceNumber) REFERENCES Teacher(LicenceNumber)
);
CREATE TABLE Student (
  StudentID VARCHAR(5) NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
  FirstName VARCHAR(40),
  SecondName VARCHAR(40),
  DateOfBirth DATE,
  ClassID VARCHAR(4) NOT NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY (ClassID) REFERENCES Class(ClassID)
);

details.title: Read a definition in order
details.text: CREATE TABLE names the relation. Each comma-separated entry defines a column or a constraint. PRIMARY KEY selects the identifier. FOREIGN KEY names the local column(s); REFERENCES names the parent table and column(s). NOT NULL makes a value mandatory. The referenced table should be available before dependent data is inserted. In SQLite, enable foreign-key enforcement for the connection with PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON before testing these constraints.
details.uz: PRIMARY KEY qatorni yagona aniqlaydi. FOREIGN KEY (...) REFERENCES ... esa mahalliy ustunni boshqa table kalitiga bog‘laydi. Bir xil ustun nomi yozishning o‘zi relationship qoidasini yaratmaydi.

details.title: Create the subject-choice relationship
details.note: ExamMark is an instructional extension used for the aggregate queries.

details.title: Structure changes
details.note: These are independent syntax examples, not a script to run after the definitions above. Do not add a second primary key. CREATE DATABASE and ALTER TABLE ... ADD PRIMARY KEY are supported in some DBMSs (for example MySQL); SQLite opens a database file instead and requires keys to be defined during table creation.

details.title: Source corrections
details.text: Use CHARACTER or VARCHAR with an appropriate length, consistently spell LicenceNumber, include parentheses around the local foreign-key columns, and keep ClassID in Student. These correct ambiguities and typographical errors in the printed examples.

worked.prompt: Activity 8G: explain how to add the teacher relationship to Class.
worked.answer: Create Teacher with LicenceNumber as its primary key. Class includes LicenceNumber of a compatible type and FOREIGN KEY (LicenceNumber) REFERENCES Teacher(LicenceNumber). The Class foreign key can repeat when one teacher has several classes.

checks.prompt: Which SQL text identifies the parent table and key in a relationship?
checks.why: REFERENCES names the parent table and its referenced key.

checks.prompt: Hodder Activity 8G: create the Teacher link for Class in words or SQL.
checks.answer: Create Teacher with LicenceNumber as primary key. Put LicenceNumber in Class as a foreign key with FOREIGN KEY (LicenceNumber) REFERENCES Teacher(LicenceNumber).
criteria: Give Teacher.LicenceNumber as the primary key.
Give Class.LicenceNumber as the foreign key.

lessons.title: SELECT: build one question at a time
lessons.subtitle: Choose columns, filter rows, then combine tables.
objectives: Select columns and filter rows.
Sort a result using ORDER BY.
Join tables through matching keys.
lessons.hook: Which students are in 7A, and how can their names be listed alphabetically?

blocks.title: Ask a question before writing SQL
blocks.text: Question: what are the first names of the students in 7A? Read the table yourself: Noor and Tahir. We will build a query that returns those two names.
blocks.uz: Savol: 7A dagi o‘quvchilarning ismlari qaysi? Jadvaldan o‘zimiz topamiz — Noor va Tahir. Endi SQL ga aynan shu savolni yozamiz.

blocks.title: First choose the column and table
blocks.text:
SELECT FirstName
FROM Student;
blocks.note: SELECT FirstName asks for the FirstName column. FROM Student tells SQL which table to use. There is no filter yet, so the result contains Noor, Ahmad and Tahir. Without ORDER BY, their display order is not guaranteed.
blocks.uz: SELECT qaysi ustunni chiqarishni, FROM esa qaysi jadvaldan olishni aytadi. Hali shart yo‘q, shuning uchun barcha ismlar chiqadi. ORDER BY yozilmasa, tartib kafolatlanmaydi.

blocks.title: Then keep only the 7A rows
blocks.text:
SELECT FirstName
FROM Student
WHERE ClassID = '7A'
ORDER BY FirstName;
blocks.note: WHERE keeps rows whose ClassID is 7A. ORDER BY FirstName sorts the names. Result: Noor, then Tahir. The text value 7A is inside single quotes.
blocks.uz: WHERE ClassID 7A bo‘lgan qatorlarni qoldiradi. ORDER BY ismlarni tartiblaydi. Natija: Noor, Tahir. Shartdagi matn qiymati bitta tirnoq ichiga yoziladi.

blocks.title: Add a second output column
blocks.text:
SELECT FirstName, SecondName
FROM Student
WHERE ClassID = '7A'
ORDER BY SecondName ASC;
blocks.note: Separate output columns with commas. ASC sorts ascending; DESC sorts descending. This result is Noor Baig followed by Tahir Hassan.
blocks.uz: Bir nechta ustun vergul bilan ajratiladi. ASC — o‘sish, DESC — kamayish tartibi. Bu safar familiya bo‘yicha tartiblaymiz: Noor Baig, keyin Tahir Hassan.

blocks.title: JOIN brings matching rows together
blocks.text:
SELECT Student.FirstName, StudentSubject.SubjectName
FROM Student
INNER JOIN StudentSubject
  ON Student.StudentID = StudentSubject.StudentID
ORDER BY Student.FirstName, StudentSubject.SubjectName;
blocks.note: Student has the name; StudentSubject has the choices. ON matches equal StudentID values. Noor has History and Maths, so Noor appears twice in this result. INNER JOIN includes only matching pairs. TableName.ColumnName makes each column’s origin clear.
blocks.uz: Ism Student da, fan tanlovi StudentSubject da. ON bir xil StudentID larni bog‘laydi. Noor ikkita fan olgani uchun natijada ikki qator bo‘ladi. INNER JOIN faqat ikkala tomonda mos kelgan yozuvlarni chiqaradi.

blocks.title: Change the class and predict the result
blocks.text: Choose 7A or 7B below. Read the WHERE condition, predict which students remain, then reveal the rows. Notice that ORDER BY still sorts their surnames.
blocks.uz: Quyida 7A yoki 7B ni tanlang. WHERE shartiga qarab kimlar qolishini ayting, keyin natijani oching. ORDER BY familiyalarni tartiblashda davom etadi.

worked.prompt: Why does the 7A SELECT return Noor and Tahir but not Ahmad?
worked.answer: WHERE ClassID = 7A keeps only the 7A rows. Noor and Tahir match. Ahmad belongs to 7B, so his row is excluded. The SQL text value must be written in quotes.

checks.prompt: In SELECT FirstName FROM Student WHERE ClassID = '7A', what does WHERE do?
checks.why: WHERE retains rows meeting the condition; ORDER BY sorts results.

checks.prompt: Write a query to show StudentID and FirstName of students in 7B, sorted by SecondName.
checks.answer: SELECT StudentID, FirstName FROM Student WHERE ClassID = '7B' ORDER BY SecondName;
criteria: Select StudentID and FirstName from Student.

recap: SELECT columns; WHERE rows; ORDER BY order.
JOIN ... ON matches related rows.
Predict row count as well as column values.
lessons.mistake: AND joins logical conditions, not the output column list. Omitting a meaningful join condition can produce incorrect combinations.
lessons.next: Next: Count marks and change records.

details.title: Here are the three Student rows
1. SELECT the columns you want
details.text:
SELECT FirstName, SecondName
FROM Student;
details.note: This request returns the names of all three students. SELECT chooses columns; FROM names the table.

details.title: 2. WHERE keeps only Class 7A
details.note: WHERE is a condition. Ahmad is excluded because ClassID is 7B. Quote the text value '7A'.

details.title: 3. ORDER BY sorts the result
details.text:
SELECT FirstName, SecondName
FROM Student
WHERE ClassID = '7A'
ORDER BY SecondName ASC;
details.note: Result in surname order: Noor Baig, then Tahir Hassan. This is Hodder's p.213 school query with a clear ASC direction.

details.title: Check the output before learning JOIN
4. INNER JOIN connects the related tables
details.text:
SELECT Student.FirstName, Class.Location
FROM Student
INNER JOIN Class
  ON Student.ClassID = Class.ClassID
WHERE Student.StudentID = 'S1276';
details.note: Student supplies Noor's name, Class supplies Room 3. ON tells SQL which key values should match.

details.title: 5. Activity 8H — students and subjects
details.text:
SELECT Student.FirstName, Student.SecondName,
       StudentSubject.SubjectName
FROM Student
INNER JOIN StudentSubject
  ON Student.StudentID = StudentSubject.StudentID
ORDER BY Student.SecondName;
details.note: One student may appear more than once: a row is returned for each matching subject choice. The source exercise asks for student names and subjects.

details.title: Check the meaning in this order
details.text: First locate the table(s), then match the join keys if there is a JOIN, apply the WHERE filter, choose the SELECT columns and inspect the ORDER BY sort. This is a way to reason about a result, not a claim that SQL databases always physically execute clauses in that order.
details.uz: Boshlanishida 1 ta jadval bilan ishlang: SELECT → FROM → WHERE → ORDER BY. Shundan keyin JOIN orqali ikkinchi jadvaldan ma'lumot olinadi.

worked.prompt: Predict the names returned by the 7A query and explain why Ahmad is absent.
worked.answer: Noor Baig, then Tahir Hassan. Both have ClassID 7A and the surnames sort Baig before Hassan. Ahmad has ClassID 7B and fails the WHERE condition.

checks.prompt: In SELECT FirstName FROM Student WHERE ClassID = '7A', what does WHERE do?
checks.why: WHERE retains rows meeting the condition; ORDER BY sorts results.

checks.prompt: Write a query to show StudentID and FirstName of students in 7B, sorted by SecondName.
checks.answer: SELECT StudentID, FirstName FROM Student WHERE ClassID = '7B' ORDER BY SecondName;
criteria: Select StudentID and FirstName from Student.

lessons.title: Count marks and change records
lessons.subtitle: Understand NULL, then INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE.
objectives: Use SUM, COUNT, AVG and GROUP BY.
Distinguish COUNT(*) from COUNT(column).
Write targeted INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE commands.
lessons.hook: Three Maths enrolments exist, but one mark is missing. How many marks should contribute to the average?

blocks.title: Two marks are known; one is missing
blocks.text: NULL means no value is stored here. It is not a mark of zero. We have three student rows but only two recorded marks.
blocks.uz: NULL — baho hali kiritilmagan. Bu 0 ball degani emas. O‘quvchilar soni uchta, mavjud baholar esa ikkita.

blocks.title: Count rows, then count actual marks
blocks.text:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS Students,
       COUNT(ExamMark) AS MarksRecorded,
       SUM(ExamMark) AS Total,
       AVG(ExamMark) AS Mean
FROM StudentSubject
WHERE SubjectName = 'Maths';
blocks.note: COUNT(*) = 3 rows. COUNT(ExamMark) = 2 non-null marks. SUM = 80 + 70 = 150. AVG = 150 / 2 = 75. AS gives each result column a readable name. NULL is excluded from these numeric inputs.
blocks.uz: COUNT(*) barcha qatorlarni sanaydi: 3. COUNT(ExamMark) mavjud baholarni: 2. SUM = 150. AVG = 150 / 2 = 75. Kiritilmagan bahoni 0 deb olib uchga bo‘lmang.

blocks.title: GROUP BY repeats the calculation for each subject
blocks.text: Without grouping, the filtered rows produce one summary. GROUP BY SubjectName makes a separate summary for Maths, History and each other subject. For a group with no recorded marks, COUNT(ExamMark) is 0 and SUM/AVG are NULL.
blocks.uz: GROUP BY SubjectName bo‘lsa, har fan alohida guruh bo‘ladi va hisob har bir guruh uchun qayta bajariladi. Guruhda birorta baho bo‘lmasa COUNT(ExamMark) 0, SUM va AVG esa NULL bo‘ladi.

blocks.title: Insert a new student
blocks.note: The values match the named columns in the same order. Quote text and ISO-formatted date values. Omitted columns need a default or permission to be NULL; mandatory foreign keys cannot simply be omitted.
blocks.uz: INSERT INTO qaysi jadvalga qo‘shishni aytadi. Ustunlar tartibi bilan VALUES dagi qiymatlar tartibi mos. Bu misolda yangi o‘quvchi S1301 7A ga qo‘shiladi.

blocks.title: Update or delete only the intended row
blocks.note: The example student has no subject-choice rows. If other tables reference a row, the FK policy governs whether deletion is allowed.
blocks.uz: Avval S1301 ning ClassID qiymatini 7B ga o‘zgartiramiz. Keyingi buyruq shu o‘quvchini o‘chiradi. Har ikkala buyruqdagi WHERE faqat S1301 ni tanlaydi. 7B Class jadvalida mavjud bo‘lishi kerak.

blocks.title: Check the target before changing data
blocks.text: INSERT adds a row. UPDATE changes values in existing rows. DELETE removes rows. WHERE limits which rows UPDATE and DELETE affect. Without WHERE, they target every row. DELETE keeps the table definition; DROP TABLE removes it.
blocks.uz: INSERT yangi qator qo‘shadi. UPDATE mavjud qiymatni almashtiradi. DELETE qatorni olib tashlaydi. UPDATE yoki DELETE da WHERE bo‘lmasa, barcha qatorlar ta’sirlanadi. Avval shu shartli SELECT bilan qaysi qatorlar tanlanishini tekshiring.
blocks.remember: Before UPDATE or DELETE, read the WHERE condition.

worked.prompt: Why is the mean of 80, 70 and NULL equal to 75?
worked.answer: Only two marks are recorded. Add 80 + 70 = 150, then divide by 2. NULL is missing, so it does not become an extra zero.

checks.prompt: What does DELETE FROM Student; do?
options: Deletes all rows, retaining the table definition
checks.why: Without WHERE it targets every row, but the table structure remains.

checks.prompt: Write an UPDATE to change only S1299’s class to 7B, then explain the FK condition.
checks.answer: UPDATE Student SET ClassID = '7B' WHERE StudentID = 'S1299'; Class 7B must already exist for the foreign-key constraint to be satisfied.

recap: Before UPDATE or DELETE, read the WHERE condition.
lessons.mistake: Do not divide AVG by all rows when some input values are NULL. Do not confuse DELETE with DROP TABLE.
lessons.next: Next: Use what you have learned.

details.title: Start with the actual exam-mark records
COUNT, SUM and AVG — do the maths
details.text: For Maths, 3 rows exist but only 2 marks are recorded. COUNT(*) is 3; COUNT(ExamMark) is 2; SUM(ExamMark) is 150; AVG(ExamMark) is 150 ÷ 2 = 75. A NULL mark is missing, not zero. COUNT(column), SUM and AVG ignore NULL inputs.
details.uz: NULL — baho qo'yilmagan. O'rtacha 150 ÷ 3 emas, 150 ÷ 2 = 75.

details.title: Ask SQL to calculate Maths statistics
details.text:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS Enrolments,
       COUNT(ExamMark) AS MarksRecorded,
       SUM(ExamMark) AS Total,
       AVG(ExamMark) AS Mean
FROM StudentSubject
WHERE SubjectName = 'Maths';

details.title: GROUP BY makes a summary for each subject
details.text:
SELECT SubjectName,
       COUNT(ExamMark) AS MarksRecorded,
       AVG(ExamMark) AS Mean
FROM StudentSubject
GROUP BY SubjectName
ORDER BY SubjectName;
details.note: History: 1 recorded mark, mean 90. Maths: 2 recorded marks, mean 75. GROUP BY forms subject groups before each aggregate is calculated.

details.title: INSERT INTO — add a new student row
details.note: A new row is inserted. Class 7A must exist to satisfy the foreign-key reference.

details.title: UPDATE and DELETE FROM — change only the right row
details.note: The WHERE clauses limit the changes to Peter's record. A referenced row may not be deletable until related rows are handled according to the database constraint policy.

details.title: Do not confuse rows with table structure
rows: Removes ALL Student rows; retains the table definition
Removes the table definition (DDL), subject to DBMS restrictions

queries.title: Who teaches each subject?
queries.sql: SELECT Teacher.TeacherName, Subject.SubjectName FROM Teacher INNER JOIN Subject ON Teacher.LicenceNumber = Subject.LicenceNumber ORDER BY Subject.SubjectName;
queries.why: The matching LicenceNumber connects each subject to its teacher.

queries.title: Who studies what?
queries.sql: SELECT Student.FirstName, Student.SecondName, StudentSubject.SubjectName FROM Student INNER JOIN StudentSubject ON Student.StudentID = StudentSubject.StudentID ORDER BY Student.SecondName, StudentSubject.SubjectName;
